summary:
S.O.R.R. is an interactive, first-person educational web application created for the Abandoned but Not Forgotten challenge. Told directly in the voice of NASA’s retired Kepler Space Telescope, the project brings space history to life for learners of all ages.
Although Kepler ran out of fuel and was switched off in solar orbit in 2018, its data continues to yield new exoplanet discoveries today. Instead of a static encyclopedia, our browser-based experience lets users fly through Kepler’s timeline—from its 2009 launch to its final day—and actively participate in its engineering struggles.
Users can play hands-on mini-games, such as stabilizing the spacecraft after reaction wheel failures, catching planetary transits on light curves, and using solar pressure during the rescued K2 mission. The platform also features educational quizzes, an exoplanet showcase, and dedicated pages highlighting Kepler’s successors, TESS and Pandora. Requiring zero installation, S.O.R.R. proves that retired spacecraft are never truly forgotten.
details:
What It Does & How It Works
S.O.R.R. is an interactive, first-person educational web application created for the Abandoned but Not Forgotten challenge. Instead of a static encyclopedia, the platform tells the story of NASA’s retired Kepler Space Telescope directly in its own voice. Users fly through an interactive timeline—from Kepler's early rejections and 2009 launch to its retirement in solar orbit in October 2018—while playing hands-on mini-games, taking knowledge quizzes, exploring discovered exoplanets, and visiting dedicated pages for Kepler's successors, TESS and Pandora.

Benefits & Intended Impact
Designed as an introductory learning experience for users of all ages, S.O.R.R. turns complex astrophysics and aerospace engineering into an approachable, memorable journey. By demonstrating that astronomers still discover new exoplanets in Kepler’s archival data today, the project shows students, educators, and space enthusiasts that retired spacecraft continue to drive scientific discovery long after powering down.

Creativity & Design Considerations
Our main creative choice was giving the spacecraft a personal voice and pairing narrative milestones with interactive problem-solving. Rather than just reading about technical failures, users actively fix reaction wheel imbalances, stabilize the K2 mission using solar radiation pressure, and detect planetary transits on light curves. We prioritized accessibility, clear visual storytelling, and zero-installation browser performance so anyone can explore the mission effortlessly on any device.

Tools & Technologies Used

  • AI-Assisted Development: The entire web application codebase, interactive mini-games, animations, and UI components (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript) were generated and built using Claude (Anthropic) based on our team's concept, prompts, educational design, and iterative testing.
  • Data & Content: Public NASA Kepler, K2, TESS, and Pandora mission archives and exoplanet light-curve datasets curated by our team.
